summary: MoonSlip is a browser-based lunar South Pole mission planning and launch-slip contingency console. At the lunar South Pole, the Sun skims the horizon at just 1.5° to 8° elevation, meaning a 10-kilometre mountain ridge can plunge a lander into weeks of darkness or sever line-of-sight communications with Earth. When launch delays (slips) occur, mission planners historically face hours of fragmented 3D GIS re-simulations. MoonSlip solves this in milliseconds: it pairs NASA JPL Horizons hourly ephemerides with 360° NASA LRO LOLA laser-altimetry topographic horizon masks across 2027–2028. It computes exact upper-limb solar and Earth clearance, generates an instantaneous GO/NO-GO verdict against lander battery and radio thresholds, and automatically ranks viable Plan B recovery dates and sites. With dual Planner and Explain modes, engineering presets, LROC QuickMap integration, and in-browser mathematical validation against NASA PGDA Product 69, MoonSlip bridges high-stakes aerospace trade studies and classroom education with open science and zero-backend compute latency.
details:
1. What exactly does it do?

MoonSlip provides instantaneous, scientifically validated answers to mission-critical lunar landing questions when orbital or rocket delays occur. Specifically, it:

·        Simulates Launch Slips:Allows planners to shift launch dates from −7 days early to +28 days late and instantly evaluates how the altered Sun and Earth azimuths interact with 3D lunar topography.

·        Delivers Instant Verdicts:Issues an unambiguous GO or NO-GO status by checking whether mission sunlight percentage, continuous night duration, Earth communication contact, and maximum silence gap meet the lander's hardware limits.

·        Ranks Plan B Options Automatically:Calculates and lexicographically sorts up to 44 alternative rescue scenarios (alternative dates at the same site and backup curated landing sites) with automated gain/loss trade-off statements.

·        Surfaces Nearest Guaranteed GO Windows:If severe launch slips cause every immediate alternative to fail, MoonSlip scans the full 731-day (2027–2028) dataset to identify and display the earliest future viable landing window.

·        Visualizes the 360° Horizon:Unrolls the entire horizon with LOLA elevation ridges, true-scale Sun and Earth discs, magnetic sunrise/sunset snapping, and side-by-side delta comparators.

2. How does it work?

MoonSlip utilizes a high-efficiency decoupled architecture:

·        Offline Precomputation:A Python data pipeline queries NASA JPL Horizons for hourly airless topocentric ephemerides (17,545 samples per site) and ray-casts Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs of NASA LRO LOLA DEMs (PGDA Product 90) in 3D spherical coordinates to create 360° horizon elevation masks at 2, 5, 10, and 20 m mast heights.

·        In-Browser Client Execution:Packaged as a lightweight ~4.5 MB static bundle, the client evaluates geometric circle-segment solar disc exposure and sub-hour linear zero-crossing interpolation via pure TypeScript functions in under 2 milliseconds, requiring zero backend compute.

·        Live Query Proxy:For custom coordinates clicked on the LOLA South Pole map, an edge rewrite proxy (/horizons-api) queries JPL Horizons in real time.

3. What benefits does it have?

·        Prevents Catastrophic Mission Loss:Recent polar missions like IM-1 Odysseus and IM-2 Athena highlighted how terrain shadows and tipping can terminate missions prematurely. MoonSlip gives mission planners immediate contingency visibility.

·        Eliminates Workflow Latency:Replaces 360 separate manual multi-step GIS/SPICE simulations with real-time, interactive exploration at 60 FPS.

·        Democratizes Lunar Science:Explain mode translates complex celestial mechanics (lunar libration, grazing solar angles, terrain occultations) into intuitive visual concepts for students and the public.

4. What do you hope to achieve?

We aim to establish MoonSlip as the standard lightweight contingency screening tool for Artemis-era lunar surface missions. By enabling rapid trade studies across lander engineering thresholds, solar mast heights, and backup landing regions, MoonSlip ensures that when launches slip, lunar science survives.

5. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

The project is engineered in React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4, Vite, and Vitest. The offline data pipeline was built in Python 3 with NumPy, rasterio, pyproj, and Pillow. Production deployment is powered by Vercel static hosting and edge API proxies.
